sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Diagnostic Dilemma: Early-Onset Thrombocytopenia Post-Cardiac Surgery
sections.description: The clinical narrative begins with a man in his seventies presenting with exertional dyspnea and a long-standing history of atrial fibrillation managed with oral apixaban. Prior to his definitive cardiac intervention, he underwent a diagnostic heart catheterization via a transradial approach. Notably, because the patient had not withheld his antiplatelet therapy, the procedural team utilized a conservative anticoagulation strategy, administering only 2,000 units of unfractionated heparin (UFH). sections.section_title: Pathophysiological Spectrum: Classic HIT vs. Autoimmune HIT (aHIT)
sections.description: To fully appreciate the complexity of the presented case, one must distinguish between the conventional pathophysiology of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) and the distinct mechanisms driving autoimmune HIT (aHIT). Classic HIT is fundamentally an immune reaction dependent on the formation of a specific antigenic complex. When unfractionated heparin (UFH) binds to platelet factor 4 (PF4), a cationic chemokine released from platelet alpha-granules, it creates large, positively charged complexes. In susceptible individuals, these complexes induce the production of pathogenic IgG antibodies. sections.section_title: Advanced Serological Interpretation: Decoding Atypical SRA Profiles
sections.description: In the diagnostic algorithm for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT), the transition from a presumptive screen to a definitive confirmation often hinges on the interpretation of complex serological data. For this patient, the journey begins with the screening immunoassay, specifically the PF4/polyanion enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). While this test possesses high sensitivity, it lacks specificity, frequently yielding false positives in the postoperative setting due to non-immune binding of PF4 to inflammatory proteins or heparin released from tissue damage. However, in this case, the optical density was 2.2 units, far exceeding the typical cutoff of 0.4 units. sections.description: The cornerstone of managing heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) is the immediate and absolute cessation of all heparin exposure, including unfractionated heparin (UFH), low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH), and even small amounts found in flushes or catheter locks. In this case, the prompt discontinuation of dalteparin and the initiation of fondaparinux were critical first steps upon recognizing the precipitous drop in platelets and the development of a new stroke. However, the clinical picture evolved rapidly into a life-threatening scenario characterized by refractory hypercoagulability.
